trace_steps: frame_retriever returns frame_21.50.png at 21.5s as the strongest problem frame (relevance_score 0.6856). OCR on the retrieved frames reads, with avg detection confidence 0.9725, “P, Q, R are centers of arcs that pass through O, the center of the circle” and “If \overparen{PQ} = \overparen{QR} = \overparen{RP}, what is the area of the shaded region?”; chart_analyzer on frame_21.50.png also reports that segment PO is labeled 6, so the circle has center O and radius 6.

Because OCR states the arcs \overparen{PQ}, \overparen{QR}, and \overparen{RP} are equal, the circumference is split into three equal arcs, so the corresponding central angles are 120° each. chart_analyzer on frame_21.50.png/33.50.png reports that P, Q, and R are equally spaced on the circle and form an equilateral triangle inscribed in the circle.

For an inscribed equilateral triangle in a circle of radius 6, each side is the chord subtending 120°, so side length PQ = QR = RP = 2·6·sin(60°) = 6√3. Thus triangle PQR has area (√3/4)(6√3)^2 = 27√3.

chart_analyzer on frame_21.50.png reports three red leaf-shaped regions, each bounded by two arcs centered at two of P, Q, R, and each arc passes through O. Since OP = OQ = OR = 6 and PQR is equilateral with side 6√3, triangle POQ (and similarly the others) is equilateral, so each boundary arc is a 60° arc of radius 6. Therefore one red leaf equals two 60° sectors minus two equilateral triangles: 2·((60/360)π·6^2) - 2·((√3/4)·6^2) = 12π - 18√3.
There are 3 congruent red leaves, so the total shaded area is 3(12π - 18√3) = 36π - 54√3. Therefore the correct choice is E.
